items_missed: Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up — opened straight into 'This is Frank. How can I help you?' and went to the calendar.

Never asked the moving-stressor question. He asked logistics-only versions ('is there anything else about the move that I need to know about?'), and the customer's own worry signals — an unbooked storage unit, a sectional that may not clear the doorway, 'I don't think we would need to remove the door frame' — drew troubleshooting but never 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?'

No 'pricing is super simple' framing. Pricing arrived as 'So in terms of like the pricing and everything, let me just make sure this checks out' — a rep talking himself through a screen, not a positioned pitch.

What's-included list was partial: 'the tools that we need the moving blankets, stretch wrap all that stuff. The truck, the Dolly's, everything.' Gas, taxes, and insurance were never named, so the customer heard an equipment list, not a no-surprises price.

**No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned** — on a job where every item gets wrapped, stacked in a shared-elevator storage unit, and left sitting for months. The customer twice asked about disassembly and stacking; the $2,000 coverage answer never came.
**Meet Your Mover never mentioned.**
**On-Time Guarantee never mentioned** — and this was an 8:30am start on a two-day pack-and-move where arrival time genuinely mattered to the customer ('I need stuff out of the house by the ninth').

No 'no hidden fees' pitch — no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees. He got close with 'you only pay for the actual time used' but never closed the loop on fees.

No sense-check after the clock and pricing block. The 2.5-hour minimum, the 15-minute proration, the $208/hr, and two separate day totals were delivered in one long stretch ending 'if we can knock this out sooner than that, then you only pay for the actual time use either day' — no 'does that make sense?'

No typical time range given for the move day itself. He gave a range for packing ('typically for your home size it takes six to eight hours') but then simply declared 'set this to maybe seven and a half hour day estimate' for the move with no range and no benchmark — and the customer pushed back on exactly that ('I think it'll take less').

**Save Your Ass prep speech essentially absent.** No consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off the walls), no 'take a carload' tip, no 'does that make sense?' close. The customer handed him the opening verbatim — 'there's some stuff that I want to set aside because I would probably like, take it with me and not in the storage. So, I'll do that like, Monday' — and Frank answered 'Okay. No, that works.' A customer volunteering to pre-consolidate on a 7.5-hour hourly estimate is the single best coaching moment on this call and it got a shrug.

Worse, he ran the SYA logic backwards on the walls: the customer offered 'I'll try to take those down as much as possible,' and Frank said 'Oh, yeah, a hundred percent... taking the stuff off the walls can absolutely do that. We can even take like, TV mounts out of the drywall.' True, but on an hourly job that talked the customer out of free prep.

**No booking attempt.** Availability was confirmed in the first minute ('it looks like we have some options for that day'), a full estimate was built, and the customer asked 'Would it be okay if I call you guys back about like official scheduling' — Frank said 'Yeah, no that's totally fine' and let it go. No 'we have the 8th and 9th open right now, want me to lock those in?'

No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections.' The reply instruction was booking-only: 'you'd simply reply back to the email and just give us the green light.'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' The customer had to volunteer the last item himself (confirming his email address).

Business hours never stated. Reachability was covered loosely — 'anyone who sees the email or even if you call in just give me your email address they'll be able to pull this up' — with no number, no hours, and no direct line back to Frank on a quote he built.

**Customer's name used zero times.** Frank spent a full minute getting 'Satwik' spelled out over a bad line and then never once used it; the only address form in 22.9 minutes was 'man' ('it really depends on how much there is to pack, man').

No Sparefoot referral despite a live, unclaimed need — 'I haven't officially booked that one so this isn't confirmed.' He coached the customer on 10x10 vs 10x15 sizing and then sent him back to Public Storage on his own.
No insurance explanation at all — neither No Worries nor the 60¢/lb baseline — on a storage job.

Efficiency: a call he framed as 'typically this takes about ten minutes' ran 22.9. Packing was relitigated three separate times, and he lost the core booking fact mid-call ('What was the date you wanted again, just to make sure I have it on the right one').
top_strength: Frank's discovery and estimate-building are the best parts of this call and they are genuinely strong. He probed the whole job without a quote form to lean on — full origin address and zip, square footage (catching the customer's own correction from 1650 down to 1335), the two-story layout, the attached garage with a follow-up when the answer was vague ('You had to guess how many are in there? Just, just so I can get an idea'), appliances, mounted items, a room-by-room inventory walk, access ('are there any other access issues that we should know about like, narrow doorways'), and the storage destination including the unbooked-unit risk: 'so you didn't get the unit yet. So we don't know the walking distance or what floor it's on.' He anchored boxes with a real benchmark instead of asking blind — 'Typically for that home size, we would see around 45 to 55 boxes. Do you have any idea if it would be more than that whether we packed or you packed?' He then explained the estimate as a model rather than a number: 'we base our estimates starting with the home size and like driving distance walking distance amount of items that need, because we're trying to calculate the time,' and flagged the one real unknown honestly — 'the storage elevator could be a factor in time. Just keep that in mind if it's a small elevator, it's gonna slow things down. If we're sharing the elevator, it's gonna slow things down.' He held the line on same-day pack-and-move rather than selling a fantasy ('typically packing takes just as long as the move portion... unless we like double the resources that's gonna make it kind of a crazy day'), and the conservative framing landed: the customer said 'I think personally, I think it'll take less but I like that you're estimating more. That's helpful.' The pad-deposit explanation was a real value-add nobody asked for, and the budget framing was authentic — 'If you have your own stuff, you know we can use that first. I'll keep the cost down but we'll bring a lot and only charge for what we use.'
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: **Frank built a complete, credible, ~$2,900 two-day estimate and then didn't ask for the business.** Availability was confirmed in the first sixty seconds, the customer was warm ('Yeah, that sounds great'), and there is no deposit standing in the way — so when the customer said 'Would it be okay if I call you guys back about like official scheduling,' the answer was not 'Yeah, no that's totally fine.' It was: 'Absolutely — but let me make this easy on you. There's no deposit, so I can hold the 8th for packing and the 9th for the move right now, and if anything changes you just reply to the email. That way the day doesn't get taken while you're deciding. Want me to put it on the books?' He gave away the one piece of urgency he had (a Wednesday-the-9th deadline and confirmed availability) for free. Second fix: **the Save Your Ass speech, and specifically the moment he inverted it.** The customer literally offered to pre-consolidate — 'there's some stuff that I want to set aside because I would probably take it with me and not in the storage. So, I'll do that like, Monday' — and then offered to pull his own art off the walls. Both got waved off. The line should have been: 'Do it, and do more of it — everything you consolidate before we show up is time off your bill. Boxes go in one spot near the garage door, loose stuff out of drawers, the art off the walls, and take a carload of the small odds and ends yourself. On a 7.5-hour hourly estimate that's the fastest money you'll save all week. Does that make sense?' Instead the customer heard 'we can even take TV mounts out of the drywall' — accurate, but it sold billable time against a rock Amanda owns (estimate accuracy). Third: **all three differentiators went unsaid on a job engineered for them.** Every item is getting wrapped and stacked in a storage unit for four-to-five months — that is the strongest No Worries setup on any call this week and it never came up: 'Everything we touch is wrapped in blankets and stretch wrap, and it's all backed by our No Worries Damage Coverage — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage.' Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee were equally free on an 8:30am two-day job. Finally, use the name. He spent a minute spelling 'Satwik' and then said 'man' instead — three uses across 23 minutes would have cost nothing. Two data hygiene items to verify in EMMA: the total was stated as '$202,898' in the transcript (the components — $1,338 packing plus $1,560 moving — do sum to $2,898, so this reads as a transcription artifact, but confirm the quote the customer received says $2,898), and the storage destination is logged as an unconfirmed address ('12318 north buck', no unit, no floor) that will need a callback before move day.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and knowledgeable — he rode out a headphone problem and a name/address spelling mess without irritation and the customer stayed positive to the end ('I think that's helpful... I will let you guys know very soon') — but the warmth was thin: zero name uses, no humor, no empathy markers, heavy filler ('you know,' 'I mean,' long strings of 'Okay. Okay. Okay.'), and 'man' as the only term of address.
audio_review_reason: Transcript has material garbling on the numbers and logistics that were quoted to the customer — the total renders as '$202,898' against components summing to $2,898, the start time as '8:39 in the morning' (likely 8:30), the storage duration as 'at least like $4 or $5' (likely 4 or 5 months), and the destination street as 'north buck' — so the actual figures the customer heard should be verified against audio and against the emailed quote before this grade is used to judge estimate accuracy.
